newsitem.title: LIBERIA: SOCCER-LIBERIANS SAY WEAH SUSPENSION RACIST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIBERIANS SAY WEAH SUSPENSION RACIST.

text.p: Liberia's sports minister claimed on Tuesday the six-match suspension of AC Milan striker George Weah by UEFA was "racially motivated."

Weah, last year's World, European and African player of the year, had a provisional one-match ban extended on Monday after a special UEFA investigation into a head-butting incident in Portugal last month.
"We believe it was racially motivated, a design to deny him a second world title because a black man shouldn't dominate the world for the second time," Francois Massaquoi told reporters.
Massaquoi, who is also Liberia's youth minister, said he would send a protest letter to UEFA and copies of the protest would be sent to newspapers across Europe.
Willard Russell, president of the Liberia Football Association, echoed his comments.
"I think the punishment was too harsh. The Portugese player was planted on Weah to provoke him because he is on the verge of becoming the world's football super-power," he said.
Weah, a FIFA fair play ambassador, admitted head-butting Porto's Jorge Costa in the players' tunnel after a Champions League game. Costa was left nursing a broken nose which later required surgery.
UEFA hinted the sanctions against Weah would have been more severe but for the Liberian's normally exemplary conduct.
The suspension does not affect Weah's role in Liberia's World Cup qualifying rounds which resume on January 10.
